newsitem.title: USA: GM CEO expects to hit '97 U.S. share goals.
newsitem.headline: GM CEO expects to hit '97 U.S. share goals.

text.p: General Motors Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Jack Smith said Thursday the automaker believes it can hit its U.S. market share target of about 33 percent in 1997, despite the declining value of the Japanese yen.
"We're still looking to be in that (33 percent) area," Smith said at a news conference following a speech at the Executives' Club of Chicago.
However, Smith said achieving the target will be more difficult than expected because of the falling yen, which gives Japanese automakers a pricing advantage in the U.S.

The yen has been falling in value and is trading in the range of 125 to 126 to the U.S. dollar. GM, which has been suffering a market share slide, finished the first quarter of 1997 with 30.2 percent of the U.S. car and truck market, down from 31.2 percent for the year-ago period.
Smith also said he does not expect a nearly two-week long strike at the company's Oklahoma City, Okla., car plant to have a significant impact on second quarter earnings.
"It's important but it's not that big. It's one plant," he said.

Smith said GM expects the yen's decline to abate and did not expect more impact from the currecny in the second quarter than in the first quarter, when the company reported net profit of $1.8 billion, up 76 percent from the 1996 first quarter, which was weakened by a strike that all but shut down the company's North American operaitons.
"Our judgment is the yen will not continue to decline," Smith said. "What was in our first quarter should repeat itself in the second quarter. We had a good first quarter."
General Motors shares were unchanged at 56-3/8 Thursday.
